definition: Present or found everywhere, or very widely.
example: Contactless payment terminals are now ubiquitous in the city.
nuance: Ubiquitous is often used comparatively; it need not mean literally every place.
prompt: A device has become a familiar sight across nearly every workplace.
options: Smartphones have become ubiquitous in everyday life.
The ubiquitous manuscript survives in just one private collection.
The ubiquitous device was unusually expensive.
reasons: This sentence demonstrates the meaning: present or found everywhere, or very widely.
A single rare instance is not widespread.
Price does not establish how widely something is found.
